title: Corium: A New ClickFix Panel Shows How Malware Delivery Is Becoming a Turnkey Business
content_md: THREAT RESEARCH / CLICKFIX / CYBERCRIME Corium: A New ClickFix Panel Shows How Malware Delivery Is Becoming a Turnkey Business A newly advertised ClickFix control panel called Corium brings together multiple malware-delivery techniques, deceptive verification pages, website injection, and conversion analytics in a single interface. Its significance lies less in inventing new attack techniques and more in making existing ones easier to manage, distribute, and potentially scale. Corium Appears on Exploit.IN A threat actor operating under the username Cassiopeia has advertised a ClickFix management panel named Corium on the Russian-language cybercrime forum Exploit.IN. The advertisement presents Corium as a platform designed to convert website visitors and advertising traffic into malware executions through deceptive verification workflows. Rather than selling a standalone fake CAPTCHA page, the developer advertises an integrated system covering payload management, landing-page creation, execution methods, campaign analytics, website integration, and notification mechanisms.
